title: P-01: PAH docking ranks and pocket contact
question: What do the stored PAH calculations show?
materials: Four original docking JSONs; six original distance XVGs; two original replicate-2 MM-GBSA DATs.
Source distance script and MD/rescoring condition notes; inputs are frozen local copies.
methods: Recalculate ranks within tool and target; do not pool scoring scales.
Summarize strict distance <0.5 nm over each finite trace and extract reported rescoring means/SD.
results: 35 docking scores; PahP first ranks: CB-Dock3: benzo_a_pyrene; Glide: anthracene; Vina: benzo_a_pyrene.
Replicate-2 MM-GBSA displayed-mean difference: 9.72 kcal/mol favouring pyrene.
conclusion: The docking methods give different first-ranked PahP ligands (CB-Dock3: benzo_a_pyrene; Glide: anthracene; Vina: benzo_a_pyrene). Pocket-contact fractions in runs 1-3 are pyrene: 19.80%, 100.00%, 100.00%; phenanthrene: 8.00%, 99.68%, 21.13%. Pyrene has the higher contact fraction in each run, and the selected replicate-2 MM-GBSA means favour pyrene by 9.72 kcal/mol.

figures.caption: Within-tool/target ranks; 1 is first. Missing methods remain absent; scores are not pooled.
All six stored finite traces; dashed line is the strict 0.5 nm criterion. Run 1 initialization differs from runs 2–3.

scope_and_assumptions: The analysis compares stored docking scores, finite initialized MD traces and one selected replicate-2 MM-GBSA result. Contact is distance below 0.5 nm. Run initialization differs, frames are correlated and CB-Dock3 shares Vina scoring. Rescoring omits entropy and uses differing salt conventions. These quantities are computational comparisons, rather than experimental affinities, equilibrium residence times or selectivity measurements.
